title: Procedure for Lung Engineering
protocol: Assemble the bioreactor components.
Sterilize all bioreactor components prior to assembly.
Connect the arterial cannula using a luer-lock fitting to a Y-splitter with a short segment of tubing.
Attach the luer-lock connector to the perfusion tubing.
Connect the unsutured segment of the Y-connector to a one-way valve for the arterial cannula.
Orient the one-way valve in the arterial cannula so that fluid can be drawn up but flows into the lung during perfusion.
Connect the tracheal cannula using a luer-lock connector linked to a Y-splitter with tubing.
Attach the luer-lock connector of the tracheal cannula to a breathing loop between the trachea reservoir and main chamber.
Connect the unsutured segment of the Y-connector in the tracheal cannula to another one-way valve.
Orient the one-way valve in the tracheal cannula similarly to that in the arterial cannula for clearing air bubbles.
Euthanize adult Fischer 344 rats by sodium pentobarbital overdose according to guidelines set forth by the American Veterinary Medical Association (60 mg/kg IP).
Spray or wipe the chest and abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Open the thoracic cavity, exposing the heart and lungs carefully to avoid damaging the lungs.
Make a small window through the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity to cause the lungs to retract.
Expand this incision horizontally to expose the bases of the lungs.
Make two vertical incisions through the ribs.
Retract the chest cage to fully expose the heart and lungs.
Prepare a gravity perfusion system using a syringe with plunger removed, a 3-way stopcock, and approximately 20cm of tubing with a 1.5-inch, 21-gauge needle.
Maintain the syringe at approximately 20cm above the animal using a ring stand.
Ensure all air is removed from the perfusion tubing.
Cut the right atrium to drain blood, preventing it from returning to the lungs.
Insert a needle into the base of the right ventricle and open the stopcock to perfuse the lungs with a solution of heparin and sodium nitroprusside in PBS.
Confirm that the pulmonary artery fills with perfusion fluid and that blood is clearing from the lungs.
Dissect the trachea free, up into the neck as far as possible.
Ensure the trachea is separated from the esophagus.
Dissect all remaining connections to the heart, lungs, and trachea, and remove en bloc.
Cut off the apex of the heart with a scalpel or sharp scissors, exposing the right and left ventricles.
Cannulate the pulmonary trunk via the right ventricle and suture in place.
Remove any excess left ventricular tissue.
Cannulate the trachea and suture in place.
Ensure that there are no air bubbles in the arterial cannula.
Place the heart/lung block into a jar containing PBS.
Use a syringe with needle to inject a small amount of PBS into the heart cannula to expel any bubbles.
Lavage the airways with PBS 4-5 times to remove as much air as possible from the lung.
Inflate the lung with PBS containing sodium nitroprusside (SNP) at 1ug/ml.
Put a stopper on the tracheal cannula so the solution remains in the lung.
Allow the lung to incubate for up to 30 minutes to permit vasodilation.
Connect heart/lungs to a bioreactor cap using luer-lock connections linked to Y-shaped cannulae.
Ensure all lines are clear of air before connecting.
Connect the pulmonary artery cannula to the perfusion line and ensure the tracheal cannula floats free.
Confirm that there is no air in the system as trapped air can prevent flow of decellularization fluid.
Inflate the lung with PBS/SNP until lungs are full, but not over-inflated.
Cap the tracheal cannula immediately after inflation.
Perfuse lung with PBS/SNP for at least 15 min at ~15 mmHg (20 cm H2O pressure).
Remove stopper from the tracheal cannula to allow the lung to deflate after perfusion.
Continue perfusion with PBS/SNP for an additional 30 minutes, refilling as necessary to maintain perfusion pressure at 10-15 mmHg.
Perfuse lung with decellularization solution (8 mM CHAPS, 1 M NaCl, 25 mM EDTA in 1X PBS) until 500 ml of solution has perfused through the lung.
Maintain optimal perfusion pressure at <15 mmHg (~20 cm H2O).
Monitor flow rates which typically start very slow (0.2-0.5 ml/minute) and increase to approximately 1 ml/minute or greater during the second hour of decellularization.
Remove used decellularization fluid from bioreactor periodically, ensuring enough fluid remains to support the lung and tracheal cannula throughout perfusion.
Transfer lung and bioreactor to a tissue culture hood.
Begin rinsing with sterile PBS by removing the jar containing decellularization fluid and replacing it with a jar of up to 1L of sterile PBS.
Use vacuum suction to ensure lines are clear of air.
Perfuse PBS through the vasculature at 10-15 mmHg.
Periodically, remove waste PBS from bioreactor and replace with fresh, sterile PBS.
Continue rinsing until at least 2.5 L of sterile PBS have perfused the lung.
Transfer lung to a new, sterile bioreactor system containing fresh PBS.
Ensure that both the entire perfusion loop and the entire airway lines are filled with fluid.
Sterilize the scaffold via overnight perfusion with PBS + 10% FBS + 10% pen-strep solution or for 3 hours with 0.1% peracetic acid in PBS.
Rinse lung with 3 changes of 250ml PBS over several hours to remove residual acid if using peracetic acid sterilization method.
Ventilate and perfuse the lung during each rinse to ensure thorough rinsing.
Transfer the lung to a 37°C incubator.
Perfuse with PBS that has 10% FBS and 10% penicillin/streptomycin for ~1hr or until temperature is equilibrated.
Treat lung with benzonase to remove remnant DNA.
Warm the benzonase buffer to 37°C.
Fill one 10 ml syringe with benzonase buffer only.
Fill another 10 ml syringe with 90 U/ml benzonase in buffer.
Stop perfusion of the lung.
Inflate the airway with benzonase buffer.
Allow the lung to deflate for approximately 1 minute.
Inflate the lung with the benzonase solution.
Avoid injecting any air into the lung during inflation.
Allow the lung to sit without perfusion or ventilation at 37°C for 1 hour after inflating with benzonase.
Resume perfusion with PBS + 10% FBS, 10% penicillin/streptomycin in the bioreactor and continue overnight.
The following day, store the lung at 4°C (for up to 3 months) or prepare it for cell seeding.
To prepare the scaffold for cellular repopulation, replace the PBS/FBS/benzonase solution with approximately 250 ml of culture medium.
Perfuse the scaffold with culture medium for at least one hour before introducing cells.
Replace the perfusion solution with fresh culture medium directly before seeding cells.
Prepare a suspension of desired endothelial cell population in appropriate culture medium.
Filter cell suspension through a 40um cell strainer to remove clumps.
Dispense cell suspension into a small reservoir incorporated into the perfusion loop of the bioreactor.
Ensure that the tubing from this reservoir and the entire perfusion loop is clear of air bubbles.
Infuse cells into the pulmonary artery at 3ml/min using a roller pump.
Continue perfusion with medium recirculated from the main bioreactor at desired rate.
Check for air bubbles in perfusion tubing daily.
Replace medium regularly, often every 3-4 days.
Prepare a cell suspension of the desired epithelial cell population.
Filter the cell population through a 40um cell strainer.
Suspend the filtered cells in 15ml of culture medium using a syringe.
Fill the airway reservoir with 80ml of culture medium.
Place the bioreactor in a 37°C tissue culture incubator.
Connect the syringe pump for ventilation.
Ensure all ventilation lines are clear of air.
Inject 15ml of cell suspension into the tracheal cannula as a single bolus.
Begin a slow breath by withdrawing 60ml of air from the main bioreactor at 3ml/minute.
Cap off the air filters on the main bioreactor immediately after injecting the cell suspension.
Allow the lungs to sit statically for approximately 18 hours.
Begin slow vascular perfusion at approximately 0.5 ml/min.
Perfuse endothelial culture typically at 1-3 ml/min using a roller pump.
Ventilate epithelial culture typically at a continuous rate of 1 breath per minute using a syringe pump.
Withdraw 5-10ml of air from the main bioreactor to induce lung ventilation at normal tidal volume.
Pause ventilation daily and exchange air in the main chamber to maintain airtight conditions.
Change medium approximately every 3-4 days during culture.
Seed epithelium for 4-8 days before seeding endothelium in co-culture experiments.
Ventilate engineered tissue while seeding epithelium, followed by perfusion and ventilation post-seeding endothelium.
Mix freshly extracted lungs with decellularization fluid.
Allow approximately 500 ml of decellularization fluid to flow through the lungs for 2.5 - 3 hours at 37°C.
Rinse lungs until PBS can flow through at about 10 ml/min under ~15 mm Hg hydrostatic pressure.
Treat lungs with 0.1% peracetic acid and benzonase after rinsing.
Store treated lungs at 4°C for up to 3 months.
Verify absence of cellular materials in the decellularized extracellular matrix.
Check DNA remnants using hematoxylin and eosin stain if necessary.
Isolate cells from 7 day old neonatal rat pups as described by Petersen and colleagues.
Expect a cell yield of 120-150 million cells per litter of 10 pups.
